utility.notes: Richmond's own MCE Clean Energy page confirms: 'PG&E will continue to deliver electricity through their power lines and provide residents and businesses with gas service.' PG&E is the underlying transmission/distribution/billing utility; MCE is a separate default generation supplier — see generation_supplier.

value.name: MCE (Marin Clean Energy) - Light Green (60% renewable, standard/default service)
value.notes: Richmond's own page states: 'Since 2013, the City of Richmond has partnered with Contra Costa County's community-based electricity provider, Marin Clean Energy (MCE)' with 'MCE "Light Green" 60% renewable energy (standard service; automatic enrollment and competitive rates with PG&E).'

county.notes: Confirmed via Contra Costa County's own official government site, which describes Richmond (North Richmond) as located within the county. No single page was found this session explicitly stating 'City of Richmond is in Contra Costa County' as one direct sentence; confidence reflects this indirect/structural confirmation, the same limitation documented for county fields in prior records this session.

permit_authority.value: City of Richmond Building Division (Community Development Department)

interconnection_url.notes: Same PG&E-wide Net Energy Metering program URL already verified for the Fremont/Oakland/Berkeley records — reused as a utility-level fact. pge.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch; confirmed to exist via search engine indexing under its expected title.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Richmond/Contra Costa County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC/PG&E-administered SGIP program already verified for the Fremont/Oakland/Berkeley records, reused here as a utility-level fact since PG&E's distribution role in Richmond is independently confirmed (S3).

value.name: Current, valid City of Richmond Business Tax Certificate (Business License)
Signed permit application ('PAF Permit Application' attachment)
Certificate of Appropriateness from the Planning Division

required_documents.notes: The Certificate of Appropriateness is required only if the project site is listed on the Richmond Historic Register.

value: Submit design through the SolarAPP+ platform to receive a SolarAPP+ Approval ID
Apply for the building permit via the City's iMS online permitting system, referencing the SolarAPP+ Approval ID
Schedule an inspection via the Automated Phone Inspection Scheduling System or electronic request
inspection_steps.notes: This is the SolarAPP+ application workflow described on Richmond's own SolarAPP+ page, not a field-inspection checklist — no separate document describing what inspectors check in the field was located this session.

value.notes: The City's own SolarAPP+ page states 'An instant permit will be created for the user when all conditions below are satisfied' (valid CSLB license, valid City Business Tax Certificate, and the required SolarAPP+/application attachments uploaded), and separately that eligible projects use 'the automated SolarAPP+ portal for instant permitting.'

eligibility_constraints.notes: Richmond's SolarAPP+ page states installations on historic resources require a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Planning Division before submitting, but does not itself state system-size caps or property-type scope; Chapter 6.47 of the Richmond Code of Ordinances likely defines these but could not be read this session (municode.com blocked automated fetch). Left null rather than assuming the common 10kW AC/single-family-duplex pattern seen in other cities without direct confirmation for Richmond specifically.
